originality.rationale: The 2021 primary source already identifies dependence on zero-mass discrepancy, and its null CLT is not new. The assessed novelty is the explicit full-support variance- and zero-matched Poisson alternative that retains exact nominal Gaussian asymptotic rejection probability despite total variation approaching one, together with a proved restricted sharp two-offset overlap coefficient. Relevant sections, tables and appendices of the primary preprint were checked. Targeted published-record and literature searches found no theorem directly implying the complete statement. Classical moment matching, CLT and Poisson local limits are acknowledged premises; unexamined historical priority remains a risk.

value.rationale: The quantified example identifies an extreme structural blind spot of a published count goodness-of-fit test: full-support alternatives can share zero frequency, mean and variance and nevertheless approach maximal total-variation separation, while the test retains only nominal Gaussian rejection probability. Explicit variance matching rules out a studentization-based explanation. The sharp optimized overlap constant makes the extremal separation quantitative and motivated. The result is not claimed to resolve optimal calibration for other tests or an unrestricted minimization problem.
